entry: Chemical element with symbol Kr and atomic number 36, a colorless, odorless [[Noble gas|noble gas]] found in trace amounts in Earth's atmosphere. The name comes from the Greek *kryptos*, meaning "the hidden one." Scottish chemist William Ramsay and English chemist Morris Travers discovered krypton in 1898 in the residue left after nearly all components of liquid air had evaporated. Like other noble gases, it is chemically inert, but its bright spectral lines make it useful in fluorescent lamps, photography and high-powered [[Laser|lasers]]. From 1960 to 1983 the official definition of the meter was based on a spectral line of krypton-86. Krypton-85, a radioactive isotope produced by the fission of uranium and plutonium in nuclear reactors, is released when fuel rods are reprocessed.

American far-right hate group that has used intimidation, violence and bombings to promote [[White supremacy|white supremacy]]. The first Klan emerged during Reconstruction, founded by former Confederate soldiers who opposed federal efforts to extend [[Civil and political rights|civil and political rights]] to formerly enslaved people. Federal Enforcement Acts and prosecutions beginning in 1871 significantly weakened it. A second Klan, founded in 1915 and peaking in the 1920s, attracted millions of members and promoted nativism, racial segregation and anti-Catholicism. A third wave arose in the mid-20th century in response to the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]]. Modern scholarship documents its extensive use of intimidation, lynching and political violence.

Capital and largest city of [[Malaysia]], a federal territory enclaved within Selangor state (pop., 2026: 2,111,536). It is the country's cultural, financial, tourism, political and economic center and is home to the Malaysian parliament and the Istana Negara, the residence of the monarch. The city was first developed around 1857 as a town serving the region's [[Tin|tin]] mines. It was the capital of Selangor from 1880 until 1978 and the founding capital of the Federation of Malaya. The federal executive and judicial branches moved to Putrajaya in early 1999. The city hosted the 1998 Commonwealth Games and [[Formula One]], and it is home to the Petronas Towers, the tallest twin buildings in the world. [[UNESCO]] named Kuala Lumpur World Book Capital for 2020.

Mongol emperor and founder of the [[Yuan dynasty]] of China (r. 1271–1294). Kublai was a grandson of [[Genghis Khan]] and succeeded his older brother Möngke as Khagan in 1260, after defeating his younger brother Ariq Böke in a civil war that lasted until 1264. He proclaimed the dynastic name "Great Yuan" in 1271 and completed the conquest of the [[Song dynasty]] by 1279, becoming the first non-Han emperor to rule all of China proper. The Yuan dynasty ruled most of present-day China, [[Mongolia]], [[Korea]] and southern Siberia. Kublai was strongly drawn to Han Chinese culture, and his reign expanded the [[Grand Canal (China)|Grand Canal]], introduced paper currency and promoted [[Silk Road|Silk Road]] trade. He ordered invasions of Japan, Vietnam, Burma and Java, and the invasions of Japan in 1274 and 1281 failed, straining resources.

Group of climbing, coiling and trailing deciduous perennial vines in the [[Fabaceae|pea family]], native to [[East Asia|East Asia]], [[Southeast Asia|Southeast Asia]] and some Pacific islands. Also called Japanese arrowroot, kudzu grows so rapidly that it smothers trees and other plants by blocking sunlight. It spreads mainly through stolons and rhizomes. Introduced to the United States in 1876 as an ornamental plant, it was promoted for erosion control and livestock forage in the 1930s and 1940s. It is [[Invasive species|invasive]] in many parts of the world, primarily North America, and is classified as a noxious weed in several states.

Disc of small bodies in the outer [[Solar System]], extending from the orbit of [[Neptune]] at 30 astronomical units (AU) to about 50 AU from the Sun. It is similar to the [[Asteroid belt|asteroid belt]] but about 20 times as wide, and most of its objects are composed largely of frozen volatiles such as [[Methane|methane]], ammonia and water. The belt is named for Dutch astronomer Gerard Kuiper, who conjectured its existence in 1951. The first Kuiper belt object found since Pluto, minor planet 15760 Albion, was discovered in 1992, and more than 100,000 objects over 100 km in diameter are thought to exist. The belt contains most of the objects generally accepted as [[Dwarf planet|dwarf planets]], including [[Pluto]], Haumea, Quaoar and Makemake. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. Studies since the mid-1990s show that [[Comet|comets]]' true place of origin is the scattered disc.

Buddhist monk, scholar and translator from the Kingdom of Kucha in present-day Aksu Prefecture, [[Xinjiang|Xinjiang]], China. He is regarded as one of the greatest translators of [[Buddhism|Chinese Buddhism]] and a pivotal figure in the development of literary Buddhist Chinese. He studied Sarvastivadin teachings, then became an adherent of [[Mahayana|Mahayana]] Buddhism and studied the Madhyamaka doctrine of Nagarjuna. After Kucha fell to the general Lü Guang, Kumārajīva was taken captive and held for years, during which he became familiar with Chinese. He settled in Chang'an around 401 under the patronage of the Later Qin dynasty and headed a team that rendered many [[Sanskrit|Sanskrit]] Buddhist texts into Chinese. He also introduced the Madhyamaka school to [[China|China]], later called Sanlun. Lu Cheng described his translations as "unparalleled either in terms of translation technique or degree of fidelity."

Hindu philosopher and scholar of the Mimamsa school in early medieval India. He wrote three subcommentaries on Sabara's commentary on Jaimini's Purva Mimamsa Sutras, including the Ślokavārttika and Tantravārttika. A staunch believer in the supreme validity of [[Vedas|Vedic]] injunction, he defended Vedic ritualism against medieval Buddhist idealism and argued that the Vedas are unauthored. His epistemology held that cognitions are intrinsically valid (*svatah pramanya*) unless proved otherwise. Some scholars classify his philosophy as existential realism. He influenced other schools of [[Indian philosophy|Indian philosophy]], and his followers, the Bhāṭṭas, held that a sentence's meaning is grasped through the meanings of its individual words. Accounts differ on his birthplace, which has been placed in South India, [[Assam|Assam]] or Mithila.

Second-largest city in [[Ghana|Ghana]] and capital of the Ashanti Region (pop., 2021: 443,981). Kumasi lies in a [[Rainforest|rainforest]] region near Lake Bosomtwe, about 200 km (120 mi) from [[Accra|Accra]], the national capital. It was founded in the 1680s by Osei Tutu I as the capital of the [[Asante Empire|Ashanti Empire]], and it remains the seat of the Asantehene. The British took over the city in 1896, after which it grew rapidly with new roads and railways. Its Kejetia Market is the biggest market in [[West Africa|West Africa]], and Kumasi is the center of Asante culture. Half of Ghana's timber processing takes place in the city. The city is also home to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital and Kumawood, a growing film industry that makes locally themed films in Twi.

[[Pilgrimage|Hindu pilgrimage]] and festival held at four sites in India: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and Ujjain. The name means "festival of the Sacred Pitcher" in Sanskrit. It is celebrated every four or twelve years, timed to the positions of [[Jupiter|Jupiter]], the [[Sun|Sun]] and the [[Moon|Moon]] in the Hindu luni-solar calendar. Hindus believe drops of the divine nectar, amrita, fell at these sites during the churning of the ocean of milk. Pilgrims bathe in rivers at their confluence to seek atonement and cleansing of sins. About 660 million people attended in 2025, up from 240 million in 2019, making it the largest gathering in the world. The first organized Kumbh Mela at Prayag took place in 1870 under British supervision. [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] has inscribed it on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Small fruit-bearing [[Citrus|citrus]] tree, or its edible fruit, native to southern [[China|China]]. The fruit resembles an orange in color and texture but is about the size of a large olive. Kumquats were cultivated for centuries in [[Japan|Japan]] and [[Southeast Asia|Southeast Asia]], and the trees are fairly cold-hardy. The English name comes from [[Cantonese|Cantonese]] words meaning "golden" and "mandarin orange." Unlike most citrus, kumquats are usually eaten whole, peel included, and the fruit is a rich source of [[Vitamin C|vitamin C]], with 44 mg per 100 g of raw fruit. Their taxonomy is disputed: they have been placed in the genus Fortunella, within Citrus, or in a single species, *Citrus japonica*. Recent genomic analysis defines three pure species, *Citrus hindsii*, *C. margarita* and *C. crassifolia*.

Mountain range in western [[China|China]], one of the longest mountain chains in Asia, extending more than 3,000 km. The range runs east from the Pamir region of [[Tajikistan|Tajikistan]] through [[Xinjiang|Xinjiang]] to Qinghai province, forming the northern edge of the [[Tibetan Plateau|Tibetan Plateau]] and the southern edge of the Tarim Basin. Its highest peak is Kunlun Goddess Peak, 7,167 m, in the western range. The Bayan Har Mountains form the watershed between the [[Yangtze|Yangtze]] and [[Yellow River|Yellow River]], China's two longest rivers. The Kunlun Volcanic Group includes more than 70 volcanic cones, which are not counted as volcanic mountains; its last known eruption occurred on May 27, 1951. In Chinese mythology, Kunlun was a semi-mythical mountain believed to be a [[Taoism|Taoist]] paradise.

Capital and largest city of [[Yunnan|Yunnan]] province in southwestern [[China|China]] (pop., 2020: 8,460,088). Kunming is nicknamed the "City of Eternal Spring" for its year-round mild climate and sits at about 1,900 m on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. It is the province's political, economic and cultural center and a major tourism center. During [[World War II|World War II]], Kunming was a Chinese military center and a transport terminus for the Burma Road, and the Flying Tigers were based at Wujiaba Airport. The city is a transportation hub linking [[Southeast Asia|Southeast Asia]] by rail to [[Vietnam|Vietnam]] and [[Laos|Laos]]. Modern growth began in 1910, when the French built the Kunming–Haiphong railway. Kunming has a nearly 2,400-year history and is home to the Golden Temple, China's largest bronze temple, dating from the [[Ming dynasty|Ming dynasty]].

Center-right [[Political party|political party]] in [[Taiwan|Taiwan]], the largest in the Pan-Blue Coalition. Sun Yat-sen founded it in 1894 in Honolulu as the Revive China Society, and it took its current name in 1919. Under [[Chiang Kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek]], it unified much of China by 1928. It later lost the [[Chinese Civil War|Chinese Civil War]] to the [[Chinese Communist Party|Chinese Communist Party]] and retreated to Taiwan in 1949. Martial law remained in effect there under one-party rule until 1987. The party's guiding ideology is the Three Principles of the People. It won the presidency under Ma Ying-jeou in 2008, and as of 2025 it is the largest single party in the Legislative Yuan.

[[Iranian languages|Northwestern Iranian]] language, or group of languages, spoken by the [[Kurds|Kurds]] in [[Kurdistan|Kurdistan]], mainly in southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, northwestern Iran and northern Syria. Kurdish varieties form a dialect continuum except for Zaza and have about 29 million native speakers. The main varieties are Kurmanji, the largest group, Sorani and Southern Kurdish. Kurmanji in Turkey is written in the Hawar alphabet, a derivation of the [[Latin script|Latin script]], while Sorani uses an alphabet derived from the [[Arabic script|Arabic script]]. Sorani is, along with [[Arabic|Arabic]], one of the two official languages of Iraq. Literary output was mostly confined to poetry until the early 20th century. The Zaza–Gorani languages, which are not Kurdish, are also spoken by several million ethnic Kurds.

Semi-autonomous federal region of [[Iraq|Iraq]] comprising four Kurdish-majority governorates: Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok and Halabja. Its capital is [[Erbil|Erbil]]. The region was de facto established in 1992 after the 1991 uprisings and the Gulf War, when no-fly zones limited Iraqi government power in the north. Iraq formally recognized it as a federal region in 2005. When the [[Islamic State|Islamic State]] advanced in 2014, Peshmerga forces took control of disputed territories. After a non-binding independence referendum in September 2017, Iraqi forces reasserted control over most disputed areas, and the region's autonomy has since eroded significantly.

Geo-cultural region of [[West Asia|West Asia]] where [[Kurds|Kurds]] form a prominent majority, sometimes called Greater Kurdistan. It roughly encompasses the northwestern Zagros and eastern Taurus mountain ranges and spans southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, northwestern [[Iran|Iran]] and northern Syria. Some definitions include parts of southern Transcaucasia, and its delineation remains disputed. The word "Kurdistan" is first attested in 11th-century Seljuk chronicles. Kurdish dynasties, emirates and chiefdoms existed from the 8th to 19th centuries. Short-lived states of the 20th century included the Republic of Mahabad in 1946. Some Kurdish nationalist organizations seek an independent state, while others campaign for greater autonomy within existing borders. During the [[Syrian civil war|Syrian civil war]], Kurds established the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, known as Rojava.

Iranic ethnic group indigenous to [[Kurdistan|Kurdistan]] in West Asia. The Kurds are a stateless nation of 30–45 million people, concentrated in southeastern Turkey, northwestern Iran, northern Iraq and northeastern Syria, with diaspora communities in Europe. Kurdish languages belong to the Western Iranic branch of the Iranic language family. The most prevalent religion is [[Sunni Islam|Sunni Islam]], with [[Shia Islam|Shia Islam]] and Alevism as significant minorities. Yazidism is the largest non-Islamic minority religion among Kurds. Demands for Kurdish independence have caused tension since the 19th century. The 1920 Treaty of Sèvres provided for a Kurdish state, but it was never ratified. The 1923 Treaty of Lausanne set the boundaries of Turkey, and the Western Allies dropped their push for Kurdish statehood. Since then, Kurdish history has been marked by struggles for independence, mainly against [[Turkey|Turkey]] and Iraq, and to a lesser extent against Iran and Syria.

Volcanic archipelago of about 56 islands in the northwest [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific Ocean]], administered by Russia as part of Sakhalin Oblast. The islands stretch approximately 1,300 km from [[Hokkaido|Hokkaido]] in Japan to the [[Kamchatka Peninsula|Kamchatka Peninsula]], separating the [[Sea of Okhotsk|Sea of Okhotsk]] from the Pacific. They form part of the [[Ring of Fire|Ring of Fire]], and the chain has around 100 volcanoes. The climate is generally severe, with long, cold, stormy winters and foggy summers. Vegetation ranges from tundra in the north to dense spruce and larch forests on the larger southern islands. The [[Soviet Union|Soviet Union]] invaded in 1945 near the end of [[World War II|World War II]], and Russia has administered the islands since. Japan claims the four southernmost islands, which it calls its "Northern Territories," a dispute that remains unresolved and impedes relations between the two countries.

American retired [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]] and Olympic gold medalist in freestyle wrestling. Angle won gold at the 1995 World Wrestling Championships and at the 1996 Summer Olympics, where he competed with a broken neck. A two-time NCAA Division I champion at Clarion University of Pennsylvania, he signed with the WWF (now [[WWE|WWE]]) in 1998 and won the WWF Championship four times. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2017. After leaving WWE in 2006, he joined Total Nonstop Action Wrestling and became its record six-time World Heavyweight Champion. [[John Cena|John Cena]] called him "without question the most gifted all-around performer."

American rock musician and founder of the grunge band [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]]. Cobain was the lead singer, guitarist and primary songwriter of Nirvana from 1987 until his death. The band's second album, *Nevermind* (1991), included the single "Smells Like Teen Spirit," which brought grunge to mainstream success. Cobain was often hailed as a voice of [[Generation X|Generation X]], a role he found uncomfortable. He struggled with heroin addiction and chronic depression. He died at his home in [[Seattle|Seattle]] from a self-inflicted shotgun wound, which police ruled a suicide. Nirvana was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame|Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2014, with Cobain honored posthumously.

Austrian-born logician, mathematician and philosopher. His [[Gödel's incompleteness theorems|incompleteness theorems]], published in 1931, showed that a consistent formal axiomatic system capable of describing [[Natural number|natural numbers]] cannot prove its own consistency and cannot decide all statements about them. Gödel proved his completeness theorem in 1929 in his doctoral dissertation at the [[University of Vienna|University of Vienna]]. He also showed that neither the [[Axiom of choice|axiom of choice]] nor the continuum hypothesis can be disproved from [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory|Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]], and he contributed to proof theory. He fled Nazi-controlled Austria for the United States in 1939 and joined the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. Later in life, believing his food was being poisoned, he refused to eat and starved to death.

German-American [[Psychology|psychologist]], a pioneer of social, organizational and applied psychology in the United States. Lewin is often recognized as the founder of [[Social psychology|social psychology]] and was among the first to study group dynamics and organizational development. His field theory expressed behavior as a function of the person and their environment, B = f(P, E). He pioneered action research, which combines empirical inquiry with practical intervention. Born into a Jewish family in Mogilno, Prussia (now Poland), he taught at the University of Berlin from 1926 to 1932. He emigrated to the United States in 1933 after [[Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler]] came to power, and he held positions at [[Cornell University|Cornell University]], MIT, [[Stanford University|Stanford University]] and the University of Iowa. A 2002 survey ranked him the 18th-most cited psychologist of the 20th century.

American author known for satirical and darkly humorous novels. Vonnegut published fourteen novels, three short-story collections, five plays and five nonfiction works. He was captured during the [[Battle of the Bulge|Battle of the Bulge]] in [[World War II|World War II]] and survived the Allied bombing of [[Dresden|Dresden]] in a meat locker at the slaughterhouse where he was held. His breakthrough was *Slaughterhouse-Five* (1969), a novel whose anti-war sentiment resonated during the [[Vietnam War|Vietnam War]]; it rose to the top of *The New York Times* best-seller list. Earlier works include *Player Piano* (1952) and *Cat's Cradle* (1963). Born in Indianapolis, Vonnegut attended [[Cornell University|Cornell University]] before enlisting in the U.S. Army in 1943. He later attended the [[University of Chicago|University of Chicago]] while working as a night reporter.

Syncretic empire of Central and South Asia (c. 30–c. 375), formed by the Yuezhi in the early 1st century. Initially based in [[Bactria|Bactria]], it spread across much of present-day [[Afghanistan|Afghanistan]], India, [[Pakistan|Pakistan]], Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. The founder, Kujula Kadphises, adopted Greek and Iranian cultural ideas, and later kings were great patrons of [[Buddhism|Buddhism]]. Under [[Kanishka|Kanishka the Great]] the armies moved north of the [[Karakoram|Karakoram]] mountains, and a road from Gandhara to China remained under Kushan control for more than a century. The empire had diplomatic contacts with the [[Roman Empire|Roman Empire]] and the [[Han dynasty|Han dynasty]] of China and was a center of trade between them. In the 3rd century it fragmented into semi-independent kingdoms, which fell to the Sasanians, and its last remnants were overwhelmed by the Kidarites and Hephthalites.
